best_for: People who write in English all day across many apps, such as support agents, marketers or non-native speakers, and want spelling and grammar help that follows them outside the browser.

points.title: Free fixes the basics
points.text: The free plan checks spelling and grammar, shows your tone without changing it, and gives 100 AI prompts a month. Sentence rewrites, tone changes and plagiarism checks are not included.

points.title: Pro is where rewriting starts
points.text: Pro is listed at USD 12 per month with a free trial and 2,000 AI prompts per member each month. It adds full-sentence rewrites, tone adjustment, plagiarism and AI-text detection, and a shared style guide. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Enterprise for company controls
points.text: Enterprise is priced by sales and adds unlimited prompts, SAML single sign-on, SCIM, data loss prevention, your own encryption keys and audit logs.

points.title: Turn it off where it does not belong
points.text: Grammarly says the desktop app works across more than a million apps, including Word, Pages, mail clients and browsers. You can switch it off for a single app or a single piece of writing, which matters for confidential documents.

points.title: Windows and Mac only
points.text: The desktop app is offered for Windows and macOS; Linux is not mentioned. The Windows installer installs for the current user in 32-bit and 64-bit builds, and the Mac disk image is universal.

points.title: A fast-moving app
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 307 versions, a sign of frequent updates. macOS lists only the current release, so going back there needs another source.
